1. Instructions for the assessment.
 i) This assessment is an individual performance.
 ii) The activity is to be done in class during the term.
 iii) It is important that the teacher facilitates the various steps of the task with learners to
 ensure active, creative and critical participation.
 iv) Read through the scoring rubrics with the learners before they begin the assessment so
 that they understand what will be expected of their final artwork. [the rubric can be printed,
 downloaded into learners’ digital devices, written out on the board or projected].
 v) Ensure the work is carried out by each learner to completion.
 vi) Encourage learners to ask questions at any time throughout the administration of the
 assessment.
 TASK CURRICULUM DESIGN(S)
 1. Grade 7 p.40 The task assesses learner’s competency in
 Strand 4.0 Indigenous Crafts • making an ornament(armlet).
 Sub strand 4.3 Ornaments • ability to design (sketch) and make an item
 • selecting reusable materials for the project

 environment. ornamental item.

 ASSESSMENT TASK: Armlet made using beadwork technique inspired by culture.
 The task requires learners to make an armlet using materials sourced from locally available
 materials inspired by culture.
 Guide the learners to;
 • carry out research on different types of armlets.
 • make several sketches of the armlet designs.
 • choose the best design from the sketches made and colour, this will help them get a colour
 scheme for the armlet.
 • collect and prepare a variety of locally available materials suitable for making the armlet.
 • use any appropriate technique to make their armlets.
 • measure their arm and add 1 in (2.5 cm) to the measurement. They measurements can be
 adjusted accordingly, depending on their choice of size since the armlets are meant for ‘sale’.
 • finish appropriately either by painting or leave it in its natural colour.
 Required materials and tools.
 • A4 size plain papers for making sketches or A4 drawing books.
 • Suitable adhesive if required.
 • Materials suitable for making beads such as inedible seeds. biro pen tubes, natural reeds,
 bamboo sticks, straws, clay, papier mâché, paper roll, cut sticks, strings (reused yarns, sisal
 strings, manilla twine, copper/aluminium wire, nylon twine) etc.
All these materials can be improvised where applicable. Schools are encouraged to reuse
materials.

2. Timelines for the project
 The following is a four-week suggested timeframe:
 FROM THE DAY PROJECT IS RECEIVED AS PER KNEC GUIDELINES
 WEEK 1
 The teacher guides the learners.
 • on the task expectations as per the scoring rubric provided.
 • to carry out research on types of armlets and materials and tools used.
 • to individually, make several sketches to come up with a design of choice.
 • choose colour schemes for the armlet and colour the different sketches.
 • collect and prepare the required materials and tools
 WEEK 2
 Guide the learners to individually:
 • build their assessment portfolios and store all sketches made; these must
 include dates when they were done.
 • start working on the project.
 NOTE: Do not buy portfolios/folders; learners are encouraged to improvise with
 materials that are locally available.
 WEEK 3 - 4
 • Production of the task continues until learners complete their work
 • Collect the final pieces and score using the rubrics,
 • records the scores and performance levels e.g., 4, 3, 2, 1 in the assessment score
 sheet provided at the end of this document, before keying the scores in the
 KNEC portal. NOTE: Print the sheets according to the number of learners per
 grade.
 • Once the scores are uploaded, hand over the assessment score sheet together
 with the all the learner’s artworks to the Head teacher/Senior teacher for
 secure storage as evidence for future reference.
 • Open guided discussion: Find out from the learners how much they would sell
 the armlets for.
 NOTE:
 The timelines suggested here are only a guide.
 • Some of the learners may require more time to complete the task than others; you may
 give these learners time to finish. Other learners may experience difficulties, break the
 tasks down in manageable steps.
 • Ensure that all learners have an opportunity to complete the tasks.
 • Learners with visual impairment could do the same task.
 • Ensure all the learners have their names on the back of their papers before storing them
 for the next session.
Schools are encouraged to carry out exhibitions to showcase the learners’ artworks at the end
of the assessment period. Take photographs or record videos as the learners carry out the tasks
and upon completion. Keep these as evidence in an ePortfolio.
